rv.q: Redcliffe, directed by Paul Foster, has huge ambition in its scope and aesthetic. There's still work to do, but our boys give their whole hearts to the story and earn ours along the way.
Luke Gage has created a masterpiece of a musical on queer love which uplifts, entertains and unites.
Redcliffe is a production that has it all to do but sticks the landing.

Above Andrew Exeter's rustic wooden plank set design, the assembled musicians deliver beautifully, resulting in a compelling and moving evening of which every contributor should feel justifiably proud.
There is a strong musical somewhere in the lives of these men, and Gage's sense of character and observational skills as a writer have laid strong foundations.
Redcliffe is a powerful drama about the persecution endured by the LGBTQ+ community across centuries.

cn.t: Critics praise this 18th-century period musical for its compelling historical story and Jordan Luke Gage's accomplished work as writer-composer, with strong performances bringing the tragic tale to life.
